make.name: Denza

logo.license: Trademark of Denza; used to identify the brand

make.description: Premium brand founded in 2010 as a BYD-Daimler joint venture; BYD took 90% in 2021 and full control in 2024. After early electric hatchbacks it relaunched with the D9 MPV (2022) and now sells large EVs and plug-in hybrids in China, Europe (from 2025-2026), Australia and Asia. It also sells Fangchengbao models abroad (B3, B5, B7, B8).

models.name: Denza EV / 400 / 500
models.description: The first Denza, an electric compact built on Mercedes-Benz B-Class underpinnings with a BYD powertrain, sold in selected Chinese cities from late 2014. It became the Denza 400 in 2016 and the Denza 500 after a 2018 facelift, and ended in 2019.

generations.name: Denza EV / 400
generations.description: Launch car (2014) and the 2016 Denza 400 with a larger, about 62 kWh LFP pack.

generations.name: Denza 500
generations.description: 2018 facelift with restyled front and rear and a 70 kWh battery.

models.name: X
models.description: Seven-seat SUV based on the second-generation BYD Tang, offered as an EV and plug-in hybrid in China from late 2020; it was dropped in 2021 and replaced by the plug-in hybrid N8.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Mercedes-styled Tang derivative; electric and plug-in hybrid versions.

models.name: N7
models.description: Electric mid-size coupe-SUV launched in China in July 2023 on the platform shared with the BYD Seal and Sealion 07; facelifted for 2024 and dropped in 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Rear-drive 230 kW or dual-motor 390 kW; up to 702 km CLTC.

models.name: D9 EV
models.description: Large luxury MPV launched in China in August 2022 as a plug-in hybrid and EV; it became China's best-selling MPV and is exported to Europe, Australia and Asia. A 2026 update moved the EV to the Super e-Platform with a 115 kWh pack.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: e-Platform 3.0 EV with a 103.36 kWh Blade battery; front-drive or 275 kW AWD.

generations.name: 2026 facelift
generations.description: Super e-Platform with a 115 kWh second-generation Blade pack and much more power.

models.name: Z9
models.description: Full-size luxury sedan launched in China in September 2024 alongside the Z9 GT, with EV and plug-in hybrid versions; the sedan ended in 2026 and was replaced by the Z9S.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Tri-motor EV with a 100 kWh Blade battery.

models.name: Z9 GT
models.description: Five-door shooting brake launched in China in September 2024 with EV and plug-in hybrid versions and BYD's three-motor torque-vectoring drive. Updated for 2026 with flash charging and up to 1036 km CLTC; launched in Europe in April 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Launch EV with a 100 kWh Blade battery and three motors.

generations.name: 2026 update
generations.description: Second-generation Blade packs of 102.3 or 122.5 kWh, rear-drive versions and flash charging up to 1100 kW.

models.name: Z9S
models.description: Shorter-wheelbase, EV-only sports sedan sold alongside (and replacing) the Z9 sedan in China from 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Second-generation Blade packs; single rear motor or three-motor AWD.

models.name: Z
models.description: Two-door electric sports car, shown as a concept in 2025 and unveiled in production form (Spider first) at the April 2026 Beijing show, with a European launch at Goodwood in July 2026. Offered as a coupe and a convertible with three motors.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Tri-motor AWD with a 76 kWh second-generation Blade pack.

models.name: N8 EV
models.description: Five-seat electric full-size SUV, the second-generation N8 (the first N8 of 2023-2024 was a plug-in hybrid facelift of the Denza X). Pre-orders opened in China on 26 October 2026 with launch set for November 2026.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: Second-generation Blade packs of 105.79 or 130.15 kWh (up to 1003 km CLTC), 320 or 370 kW rear drive or 890 kW tri-motor AWD, flash charging.

models.name: N8L EV
models.description: Six-seat full-size SUV launched in China in October 2025 as a plug-in hybrid; a battery-electric version followed on 14 September 2026.

generations.name: First generation (EV)
generations.description: EV with a 130.15 kWh second-generation Blade pack, 370 kW rear motor and 10-97% charging in 9 minutes.

gaps: Denza X EV and N7: per-variant battery, power-to-range mapping and prices not sourced.
Denza Z: power output reported inconsistently (target 1000 hp vs a 1180 kW figure); left null. UK price reported as GBP 142,900 but not tied to coupe or spider.
Denza N8 (2026): pre-sale prices not yet published; battery-to-range mapping not given.
D9 EV and Z9 GT export prices (EUR/AUD) not collected; D9 EV WLTP figures are from the Singapore catalogue.
